debate.text: Aldmere had 14 veterans on the street and £420,000. Answer A was the only one that passed every ask: ten hostel beds by 1 December, four repaired flats by 15 December, a named support worker for a year. I adopted it as written. Keys by Christmas, and someone still knocking in June.

Eighteen flats repaired is eighteen flats someone has to heat. I want the repair bill to say what a household pays per year to keep one warm, or the first cold snap undoes the good work. Cheap to insulate now, dear to fix later.

A named worker visiting weekly is the right call. Plenty of veterans sleep rough because of what they carried home from service. Bea, make sure that worker can get a veteran seen by a doctor, not just handed a leaflet.
Fair on both. The jury also split the other 14 flats half to families, half to rough sleepers, and I will hold to that. Nobody on the list moves down for a veteran.

changes.text: Veterans sleeping rough get a bed by Christmas, a named support worker for 12 months, and a published sum for every part of the money.
changes.why: Aldmere's answer A passed every test, with dates, costs and January homes.
